problem: Open-vocabulary semantic mapping methods (ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG) are offline, slow, and static, while dynamic-SLAM methods handle only short-term motion; naively plugging intermittent, view-dependent foundation-model detections into mapping causes identity drift and stale semantics. No prior system is real-time, open-vocabulary, instance-level and handles both short- and long-term changes.
motivation: Robots given open-vocabulary language goals (e.g. 'the chair that was near the plant earlier') need an object-centric map that keeps instance identities and relations valid as objects are occluded, moved, removed or added. A queryable, up-to-date scene graph also lets a VLM reason without raw video or point clouds.
key_idea: Combine high-frequency LiDAR-inertial-visual SLAM with asynchronous GroundingDINO+SAM2 detections, fused through 3D-aware tracking, geometric (depth-residual) consistency and Bayesian label updates, into a real-time queryable 4D scene graph that a VLM uses for language-guided navigation.
insight: Identity persistence and stale-content removal come from tying 2D tracks to the 3D map (projected centroids as Kalman priors) and re-checking map points against new depth and semantic evidence. In the ablation (41 annotated objects) removing the 2D tracker, semantic fusion or geometric consistency drops F1 from 0.6308 to 0.5780, 0.5201 and 0.5764; semantic fusion matters most for recall. Compared with raw video, serialized scene graphs give the VLM better spatial and temporal reasoning, though this is shown only qualitatively.
method: Geometric layer: SuperOdometry gives onboard LiDAR-inertial-visual pose P_t = T_WB·T_BC and a colorized dense 3D reconstruction, which anchors all detections in metric space.
Instance detection and segmentation: GroundingDINO detects objects from a pre-defined prompt list and SAM2 produces masks; the masks are unprojected with depth and pose into 3D object candidates.

3D-to-2D motion-compensated tracking: a ByteTrack-style Kalman tracker whose predicted centroid is the projection of the map instance's 3D centroid under the current pose, keeping IDs through occlusion and fast ego-motion.

Probabilistic geometric consistency update: the depth residual Δd = projected depth − sensor depth classifies map points as observable, unobservable (behind a surface) or disappeared (in front); log-odds updates penalize dynamic points so moved or removed objects are pruned.

Bayesian semantic fusion: each instance keeps a categorical label posterior updated with the detector confusion matrix; objects whose belief falls too low are removed, suppressing transient misclassifications.

4D scene graph: nodes are instances; spatial edges (on, beside, under) come from class-dependent geometric predicates over clustered objects; temporal edges link the same instance across time to trace trajectories.

VLM interface: a local subgraph is serialized to text (ID, label, 3D centroid, relations, schema); the VLM returns target instance IDs in <answer> tags, and their centroids become navigation waypoints.

setting.backbone: GroundingDINO + SAM2 (frozen) for perception; SuperOdometry for SLAM; Gemini 2.0 Flash (frozen) for scene-graph reasoning
setting.observation: Livox Mid-360 LiDAR + IMU + panoramic RGB camera (RGB-D or point-cloud video for benchmarks)
setting.action_space: 3D goal waypoints (object centroids) passed to the robot's navigation stack
setting.simulator: ScanNet offline sequences for mapping benchmarks; real world for the rest
setting.privileged: none (pre-defined list of object prompts for detection is required)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark was evaluated. Results are ScanNet class- and instance-level segmentation, a self-collected change-detection experiment and qualitative VLN demos, so none map to the canonical benchmark list.
results: On ScanNet class-level segmentation SuperMap gets Acc 55.48 and f-mIoU 43.50 (without background), second to RayFronts (Acc 56.76) and above ConceptGraphs and HOV-SG. Instance-level results are far better than HOV-SG and ConceptGraphs, e.g. chair mAP50 63.76 vs 4.58 and 0.00. In real-world change detection it beats DualMap (near-zero detection recall) and Khronos (failed). Runtime is 10 Hz pose, 1 Hz 2D segmentation, 3 Hz mapping and 5 Hz scene graph. VLN is shown only qualitatively.
limitations: Depends on a pre-defined object prompt list for open-vocabulary detection, so it cannot handle truly novel objects; tracking of highly dynamic objects is limited.
Evaluation is small and mostly qualitative: six changed objects in one environment, one 41-object ablation scene, no quantitative VLN success metrics or standard VLN benchmarks.
2D segmentation runs at only 1 Hz and memory is higher than ConceptGraphs (about 2 GB vs 0.86 GB); class-level mIoU trails RayFronts.
